entities.summary:
Ageladas was a celebrated Greek (Argive) sculptor, who flourished in the latter part of the 6th and the early part of the 5th century BC.

He is best known for his works at the temple of Apollo at Delphi, including the famous statue of the Apollo of Delphi, which is now considered a masterpiece of ancient Greek art.

Ageladas' innovative use of the 'Hellenistic style' of sculpture, characterized by naturalism and emotion, influenced generations of Greek sculptors, including the renowned artist Phidias.

The exact dates of Ageladas' life are unknown, but his works demonstrate a mastery of technique and a deep understanding of human emotion, which continue to inspire artists and art lovers to this day.

Ageladas' legacy extends beyond his own works, as his innovations in sculpture paved the way for the development of Western art, shaping the very course of human expression.
